Not published.** Krista Loughton · Council · incumbent. Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom and is Joa's to apply or reject. Incumbent rule applied: Record shown in the cell; a sourced miss caps below Close. Alignment compute APPLIED letter for Loughton stays **D** until Joa clicks. **Re-scored 2 Sep 2026, second pass.** First pass scored 10 cells off the home page and /priorities only. This pass adds **/kristadelivers** (the campaign's own record page, missed on pass 1), the **City of Victoria eSCRIBE minutes corpus (Nov 2022 – Aug 2026, \~370 agendas and minutes)**, and 2026 news quotes. Two FLAGged roll-calls are now resolved from the official record. n moves 10 → 21. The internal proposal stays **C**. ## Card

**Standing evidentiary caveat for every June–August 2026 item on this card.** The City has published no Committee of the Whole or Council minutes since **11 June 2026**. Everything after that date (25 Jun amalgamation, 23 Jul cooling, 30 Jul medetomidine and by-name list) rests on the published **agenda** plus media, never on a recorded division. Separately, Victoria's minutes stopped naming movers and seconders after **22 February 2024** — from 7 March 2024 every motion reads only "Moved and Seconded". Minutes name only those **opposed**, plus a full attendance list, so a Loughton YES after Feb 2024 is usually derivable by arithmetic but not stated. Cells say which basis they use. ### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **record** Voted YES on the 2026 budget (7.28% overall / 9.34% residential): "OPPOSED (3): Councillor Gardiner, Councillor Hammond, and Councillor Kim / CARRIED (6 to 3)", all nine present. In 2023 she **moved** the motion that raised that year's increase: "allocate an additional \$500,000 to the 2023 City budget, bringing the property tax increase to approximately 6.3%". No cap, formula or glide path anywhere in 2026. "Fairer taxes" is regional police cost-sharing, scored on row 33. [minutes 2026-05-07](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=108010) · [minutes 2023-04-06](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=90287) votes 2026-05-07 and 2023-04-06 · retrieved 2026-09-02
Downtown order M26 / M27 **said** "Continue OUR DWTN for cleanliness and safety, to support arts, culture and events, and increase foot traffic to local shops." No Public Order Team, no unified command, no 6am–10pm bylaw hours, and **no 2026 statement of any kind on bylaw enforcement**. Record on the same door: she moved the 2023 and 2024 motions funding the VicPD Downtown Late Night Task Force and downtown foot patrol (row 6). [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities) retrieved 2026-09-02
Housing M6 **said** "Continue to champion affordable housing by prioritizing non-profit and workforce housing to ensure renters, families, and seniors can continue to live in Victoria." Her record page claims "Victoria has surpassed provincial housing targets, approved approximately 9,000 new homes (50% rental and 20% affordable)". No unit target of her own and no 25/20/15 composition split. Counterweight in the same window: Times Colonist, "Victoria falls below target for medium and low-income housing". [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-falls-below-target-for-medium-and-low-income-housing-12448806](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-falls-below-target-for-medium-and-low-income-housing-12448806) retrieved 2026-09-02 · press 2026-06-21
Household bill M66d **—** Researched silence, not unresearched. Water, sewer, stormwater, the combined household number, CRD water rates and the \$1.07B Goldstream filtration plant appear **nowhere** in her 2026 campaign site, motions or press. She is asking voters for a CRD Director seat with no published position on the regional bill. — —
Written program — **yes** Authorized 2026 site ("Authorized by Charlene Bart, financial agent") with a three-pillar priorities page and a delivered-record page. Not costed, no targets, no dates. **Internal contradiction:** the home page and the survey page both say "Councillor Loughton will be using your vital feedback to inform her 2026 campaign platform", while /priorities presents a settled platform with no provisional caveat. Her **VoteMate 2026 profile is blank** ("hasn't uploaded a profile yet") and the X account her own footer links to returns **404**. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities) · [https://votemate.org/bc2026/candidates/13551](https://votemate.org/bc2026/candidates/13551) retrieved 2026-09-02
--- ## The 12 topics No topic gets its own letter. Area columns stay blank. Rules as written on . Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date**. A dash is unknown, not a fail. 📋 Record is shown, not scored, and does not add to n. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Partial+ 1.5** "Victoria has surpassed provincial housing targets, approved approximately 9,000 new homes (50% rental and 20% affordable), and adopted the new OCP to guide future growth". · Commits (action taken) with a stated composition mix, plus the forward line "Continue to champion affordable housing by prioritizing non-profit and workforce housing". Comparable instrument: a composition claim and the Affordable Rental Housing Revitalization Tax Exemption ("10% of units renting at 30% of median income — about \$1,400 instead of \$2,100 for a new one-bedroom"), not M6's competitive land disposition or 25/20/15 targets. **Capped below Close by a sourced miss on the same measure:** Times Colonist, 21 Jun 2026, "Victoria falls below target for medium and low-income housing", against her own page's "surpassed provincial housing targets". Record, matching, not a second mark: named YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers) · [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-falls-below-target-for-medium-and-low-income-housing-12448806](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-falls-below-target-for-medium-and-low-income-housing-12448806) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · press 2026-06-21 · vote 2023-01-26
2 M6b land bank + co-ops **📋 Record** "The City's Housing Reserve Fund invested \$5.4 million to support 475 new homes at sites like 926–930 Pandora, Wellness House, and Village on the Green." · A City capital fund deployed to non-market projects, claimed on her record page. Not scored: it is not a land bank, there is no parcel-level public inventory, no strategic acquisition fund, no competitive disposition scored on speed and design, and no right-of-first-refusal for non-profit or Indigenous housing partners. Does not contradict a 2026 promise, so 📋, not a mark. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers) retrieved 2026-09-02
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening **Close 2.0** "The Fast Track for Affordable Housing program helped speed up the application processing time to deliver these projects faster." · Commits (action taken); same page claims the City "sped up approvals (especially for non-market and rental housing)". Comparable instrument: Fast Track is a tenure-based priority stream, which is one of M7's own listed instruments. Not Aligned: **no published permit times by category, no service standard, no quarterly variance report, no one-stop centre, no AI pre-screening** — and M7's flagship claim is the publication, which she has never made. Absence of a benchmark is Record, not a cap, so Close stands. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers) retrieved 2026-09-02
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved designs, an architectural competition and an unamended-design expedited stream do not appear anywhere in the 2026 material. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty — No vacancy target, no DCC reduction position, no secondary-suite amnesty, no permitting concierge. The Revitalization Tax Exemption is scored on row 1. — —
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team **📋 Record** **Moved By Councillor Loughton / Seconded By Councillor Thompson** — "a. For one time only, the Downtown Late Night Task Force, up to \$220,000 … b. A VicPD downtown foot patrol project to add increased police presence to the downtown core, at \$35,200" (CARRIED 7 to 2, 6 Apr 2023). She moved the same task force again on 29 Jan 2024 (\$280,000). Not scored: a late-night police task force is not M26's unified operation — no VicPD + Bylaw + Public Works + Outreach single command, no 8 AM briefing, no single field supervisor, no co-located desk, no weekly DPOT dashboard. The **foot patrol** instrument is scored once, on row 12. Does not contradict a 2026 promise. [minutes 2023-04-06](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=90287) votes 2023-04-06 and 2024-01-29 · retrieved 2026-09-02
7 M26b civilian crisis response **Close 2.0** "Mental health outreach expanded this term through the Co-Response Team, a partnership between Island Health and VicPD, and Crisis Response, Community Led (CRCL), a civilian-led mobile team providing trauma-informed care during mental health crises." · Commits (action taken; "Councillor Loughton led advocacy work for the Province to better align outreach teams with housing pathways and recovery supports"). Comparable instrument: a civilian-led mobile crisis team exists and she advocates for it, but there are **no published dispatch criteria agreed with VicPD, Fire, BCEHS and Island Health, and no published diversion figure**, and it is not dispatched from an M26 co-located board she does not have. Context, her own named 2026 motion, not a second mark: co-author with Coun. Hammond of "Emergency Response to the Medetomidine Crisis" (30 Jul 2026) asking the Province and Island Health for "Dedicated resources for frontline outreach" and "Immediate, on-demand pathways to treatment and recovery services" — M26b's own advocacy-at-zero-cost fallback. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers) · [COTW agenda 2026-07-30](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=108448) · [https://cheknews.ca/motions-calling-for-emergency-response-to-sedative-in-drug-supply-and-action-on-fugitives-on-victoria-streets-pass-unanimously-1339608/](https://cheknews.ca/motions-calling-for-emergency-response-to-sedative-in-drug-supply-and-action-on-fugitives-on-victoria-streets-pass-unanimously-1339608/) retrieved 2026-09-02 · motion dated 2026-07-27, meeting 2026-07-30
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — **Researched silence.** No bylaw-enforcement hours, no staffing number, no deployment rule, and no 2026 statement on bylaw enforcement in any campaign page, motion or press item found. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — No focused-deterrence model, no Crown coordination on prolific offenders, no weekly hotspot publication. **Do not attribute:** the 30 Jul 2026 "Advocacy to improve return of fugitives wanted on warrants" motion is **Coun. Thompson and Mayor Alto**, signed by them, not her. HIFIS is homelessness data, scored on row 22. Her medetomidine motion is scored on row 7. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws **📋 Record** FLAG from pass 1 now resolved from the official record. 18 Jul 2024, main motion as amended: "direct the City Manager … to put an end to illegal daytime temporary sheltering in Victoria parks and on city streets, sidewalks and boulevards" — "OPPOSED (1): Councillor Kim / CARRIED (8 to 1)", nine present, so **Loughton voted yes**. Balancing fact from the same meeting: she was among the four who **supported softening** the wording to "continue to try to put an end to" — "OPPOSED (5): Mayor Alto, Councillor Coleman, Councillor Dell, Councillor Gardiner, and Councillor Hammond / DEFEATED (4 to 5)". Continuity in 2026: "I have been doing everything I can this term to get people moved indoors, because tents are not a solution to homelessness." Not scored: this is a 2024 action with no 2026 bylaw-enforcement promise to contradict. [COTW minutes 2024-07-18](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=99459) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/bc-supreme-court-finds-victoria-has-authority-to-restrict-camping-in-city-parks-12416801](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/bc-supreme-court-finds-victoria-has-authority-to-restrict-camping-in-city-parks-12416801) vote 2024-07-18 · press 2026-06-14 · retrieved 2026-09-02
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) **📋 Record** 2 Jul 2026: the motion to close the supervised consumption site at The Harbour **failed with only Coun. Gardiner in favour** — she did not support closure. Reported speech, not a quote, so not scored as a sentence: "It's not about what's happening inside The Harbour, it's about what's happening outside, said Coun. Krista Loughton". Not scored: buffer zones, a protected list of child-focused spaces, and CDSA coordination do not appear. Does not contradict a 2026 promise. [https://vicnews.com/2026/07/02/motion-to-close-safe-consumption-site-in-victoria-fails/](https://vicnews.com/2026/07/02/motion-to-close-safe-consumption-site-in-victoria-fails/) vote and press 2026-07-02 · retrieved 2026-09-02
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting **Aligned 3.0** "Led the creation of the Housing Relocation Program which moved 75+ people indoors, and out of encampments in Stadacona, Topaz, Irving and Vic West parks — and the work is ongoing throughout the city." · Commits, same instrument on two of the four: **M35 capacity-first** — "people who were staying at city parks that were subsequently closed to overnight camping were offered housing through a city-funded team before the parks were closed to camping. To date, that team has housed more than 70 people" is M35's "build capacity first, then enforce, and never move people to nowhere", verbatim in substance; **M36 visible presence** — "downtown foot patrols (Councillor Loughton led reviving this with VicPD's Chief Constable in early 2023)". Cluster misses M37 all-night lighting entirely and has no written same-day removal protocol (M34). Distinct sentence from Positive Flow, which is row 23; distinct from the Late Night Task Force, which is row 6. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities) · [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/bc-supreme-court-finds-victoria-has-authority-to-restrict-camping-in-city-parks-12416801](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/bc-supreme-court-finds-victoria-has-authority-to-restrict-camping-in-city-parks-12416801) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · press 2026-06-14
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Opposed −1.0** Five Year Financial Plan Bylaw 26-040, 7 May 2026: "OPPOSED (3): Councillor Gardiner, Councillor Hammond, and Councillor Kim / CARRIED (6 to 3)" — nine present, so a Loughton YES on 7.28% overall and **9.34% residential**. Disagrees with a capped residential glide path. Compounding action: on 6 Apr 2023 she **moved** "allocate an additional \$500,000 to the 2023 City budget, bringing the property tax increase to approximately 6.3%", and voted to defeat the Coleman/Gardiner amendment that would have funded it from contingency instead of a tax increase. Context, same debate, not a second mark: she voted "with a heavy heart" — "The public must understand the staggering cost of our current direction. We are paying a crisis premium for services that manage the symptoms of an issue rather than solving the cause." 2026 "fairer taxes" is scored on row 33. [minutes 2026-05-07](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=108010) · [minutes 2023-04-06](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=90287) · [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) votes 2026-05-07 and 2023-04-06 · press 2026-05-11 · retrieved 2026-09-02
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule **📋 Record** 3 Mar 2026, part 1 of the mayor's motion: "Approve reducing the 2026 debt reduction allocation to zero" — "OPPOSED (3): Councillor Kim, Councillor Caradonna, Councillor Gardiner / CARRIED (6 to 3)", nine present, ratified identically 12 Mar 2026. The financial plan shows the zeroed line as **\$2,000,000**, and \$5,500,000 of the \$5,700,000 recovered was directed "to reduce the property tax increase". **Why this is Record and not Opposed:** M66c makes the scheduled debt-reduction contribution unavailable as a balancing item *absent a 6-of-9 supermajority with a published rationale* — this vote was 6 of 9 in open session, so it clears M66c's own override rather than breaching it. Not scored: no over-collection refund rule, no published debt ceiling, no quarterly debt metrics. She is **not named**; the yes is derived from a complete attendance list and a named opposed list. [Special COTW minutes 2026-03-03](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=107164) · [Council minutes 2026-03-12](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=107836) vote 2026-03-03, ratified 2026-03-12 · retrieved 2026-09-02
15 M66d the Household Bill — **Researched silence.** Water, sewer, solid waste, stormwater and a single combined household figure appear nowhere. "Make Victoria More Affordable" is housing and police cost-share, scored on rows 1 and 33. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger **Close 2.0** "Hold all CRD municipalities accountable to host their fair share of supportive services for the homeless. Victoria cannot continue to carry the load alone." · Commits, and backed by a sourced 2026 instrument: her 12 Feb 2026 motion asked staff "to work with BC Housing and the Capital Regional District to develop a regional positive transfer system for supportive housing", and the 5 Feb 2026 direction was "to work with the CRD, BC Housing, and other partners in developing a potential cost shared STEP-like positive flow pilot" (CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY). Comparable, not same: **no quarterly downloading ledger, no twice-yearly UBCM/FCM resolutions, and no published refusal threshold** naming what Victoria will not assume without indexed funding — which is precisely the instrument her own "cannot carry the load alone" argument needs. Running for CRD Director is office-seeking, not a source; the sentence and the motions are. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities) · [COTW minutes 2026-02-05](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=106674) · [COTW minutes 2026-02-12](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=107163) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · votes 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-12
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — **Researched silence, and the sharpest gap on this card.** No statement located on regional water rates, sewage, the CRD operating or capital budget, or the \~\$1.07B Goldstream filtration plant — checked against her campaign site, her motions, and the two Times Colonist water-rate and water-DCC pieces (1 Nov 2025, 13 Feb 2026), neither of which mentions her. Her only sourced CRD content is homelessness cost-sharing (row 16) and HIFIS (row 22). She is seeking a CRD Director seat. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Close 2.0** "Work with the business community to develop an economic development plan and retail strategy." · Commits. Comparable instrument for **M73d**, a Council-adopted Strategic Economic Plan, reinforced by "Pragmatic support for downtown businesses, recognizing that a thriving downtown benefits the entire region." Not Aligned: **no storefront vacancy number (11% → 5%), no quarterly vacancy report by block, no one-mandate-not-a-new-office construction, no Conference Centre target or net cost, no employment-lands inventory.** OUR DWTN is scored on row 26; the non-profit grocery bullet is not a measure in this 55. [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/priorities) · [https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers](https://www.kristaloughton.ca/kristadelivers) retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — No capital-approval threshold, no 15-minute meter grace, no parking position, no homeowner permit-fee schedule. Crystal Pool is Record on row 50. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. — Standard lək̓ʷəŋən land acknowledgement in the site footer, and "Supporting community events like the South Island Powwow". Neither is a source: **no government-to-government working table, no 5% Indigenous procurement standard, no dual place-naming programme, no cultural protocols for City operations, no urban Indigenous services liaison.** Also not a source: the July 2024 amendment adding "Indigenous Peoples" to the sheltering conversation is a consultation-inclusion amendment, not an M1–M5 instrument. Filmmaker background and CCCO presidency are not a source. — —
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Aligned 3.0** "I think it's really important that we do everything we can to keep temperatures under 26 degrees in rental buildings. And based on the last heat dome and the loss of life, we just need to do everything we can." · Commits, **same instrument and same number as M64**: the 14 May 2026 motion directs staff to "Explore the tools available for the City to adopt a bylaw, or modify an existing bylaw, that restricts landlords from prohibiting cooling equipment, and/or requires existing rental units to have a heat pump, or other cooling equipment or passive means, that prevents at least one room of the unit from exceeding the standard recommendation of 26 C (79 F)" — M64's exact two-step sequence and its Standards-of-Maintenance-Bylaw hook. She is **named** among the eight who refused to postpone it ("OPPOSED (8): … Councillor Loughton … / DEFEATED (1 to 8)"), and on 23 Jul 2026 she **moved the carried passive-cooling amendment**. Second same-instrument hit on M9: co-author, with Couns. Thompson and Caradonna, of "Increasing Protections for Victoria Renters" (28 May 2026, passed unanimously), asking staff to report on "the first year of the Tenant Protection During Redevelopment Bylaw and whether it may be necessary to strengthen it" and on "options to improve compliance with the Rental Property Standards of Maintenance Bylaw". Her quote: "Expanding tenant supports isn't just about stability; it is vital to homelessness prevention." Context, not a second mark: unanimous 3 Mar 2026 vote for "\$100,000 to the Community Social Planning Council for its Rent Bank program". Cluster miss: **M9b short-term rental licensing is absent entirely.** Note for the Program, not a mark: the same motion asks staff to report on "rent control and vacancy control measures", which v1.10 declined as a provincial RTA file when M9c was dropped. [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-takes-steps-to-remove-barriers-to-cooling-devices-in-rentals-12593631](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-takes-steps-to-remove-barriers-to-cooling-devices-in-rentals-12593631) · [COTW minutes 2026-05-14](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=107898) · [COTW agenda 2026-05-28](https://pub-victoria.escribemeetings.com/FileStream.ashx?DocumentId=107674) · [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/25/victoria-considers-suite-of-rental-support-policy-options-to-explore/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/25/victoria-considers-suite-of-rental-support-policy-options-to-explore/) votes 2026-05-14, 2026-05-28, 2026-07-23 · press 2026-05-25 and 2026-07-24 · retrieved 2026-09-02
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists **Close 2.0** "That Council direct staff to work with community and government partners as needed to set up a By Name List for the unsheltered homeless population in the City of Victoria and report on its status monthly to Council." · Commits — she is the **named author** on the agenda ("From: Councillor Krista Loughton"), and the amended motion passed unanimously 30 Jul 2026. Her framing: "by name lists moves us from guessing how many people are experiencing homelessness once a year to knowing every individual by name in real time so we can connect them to the exact housing and support that they need." Comparable, not same: a real-time by-name list with monthly reporting is **not** M10's single digital portal with published point-based scoring, visible queue position and a no-outside-intervention rule. HIFIS entered by floor amendment, not in her written motion. Staff report back 3 Sep 2026.
